verdict.rationale: LangGraph's interrupt() mechanism explicitly lets a graph pause execution at any node (e.g., a node calling a sensitive tool) and wait for external input, resuming only via Command re-invocation — this is the standard pattern for gating tool calls on human approval, and checkpointers back this with durable state. GitHub feature list and docs independently confirm 'Human-in-the-loop — seamlessly incorporate human oversight... at any point during execution,' and community commentary (HN) corroborates LangGraph as providing 'a state machine framework for human in the loop.' missing for 10: a first-party worked example specifically gating a tool-call node (vs. generic interrupt points), and independent hands-on validation of the approval-before-tool-call pattern.
